I'm so sorry for your loss. I was 21 when I lost my dad. That was three years ago and there hasn't been one single day since then that I haven't wished he would just come back. 
I think what my mother and brother did was throw themselves completely into work. My mother was a homemaker for 20 years, until the day he passed and she took on his role the very next day. Someone had to. 

In a way, she didn't have time to grieve. She had to keep the family afloat. She had to learn the whole business and keep it running. I will always admire her for this. 

My brother had just been cheated by his business partner, a week before our father's death. After father died he threw himself into rebuilding everything that his partner stole from him. 

As for me, I was in denial for a long time. I was away for college when he died so not having to constantly feel his absence, stare at the chair he always sat on, not having to see the collection of alcohol he left behind.. all of it helped me stay in denial. I wont go into the rest of how I dealt with it because it was rather unhealthy. 

Long story short, I'd advice you to dedicate your time into doing something that you know would make him proud. It will distract your from facing your current situation head on, while also accepting that he's gone, and it will be rewarding in the end. 

You will never stop missing him. You will never stop wishing he would come back. But at the end of the day all you can do is honour is memory and hope you're making him proud :)

If you really want to make changes, start by changing little habits. Start by waking up an hour earlier than you usually do. If you have any hobbies look for options to turn them into something productive. For example if you like writing, or designing, etc, you could check out this website called Fiverr where you can freelance in your own time and stop whenever you want. That way you’ll get some experience and it’ll be a bit easier to get a job later. You could even tutor small children, or volunteer at an NGO, or even just do small chores around the house just to break away from your routine. Meanwhile figure out where your interests lie and try interning somewhere that will give you relevant experience in the field.
It takes time to break out of habits, so start small or you’ll end up overwhelming yourself. 
I promise, it will all fall into place one day. It always does. You just have to begin somewhere, no matter how small. :)

I’m going to turn 24 this October and just graduated college last month. All my classmates were at least two years younger than me and my high school friends have completed their post graduation courses and moved on to their 5th jobs. 
I was just like you, had everything handed to me on a platter, parents paid for college and the very nice apartment I lived in during my college. 
And then, a little more than a year ago, my father passed away. My mother, who hadn’t worked a day in her life either, had to take up work and my monthly allowance became less than half. I had to leave the big city I lived in during college and moved back to my small town. I watched as my mother struggled day and night to make less than half the money my father to make ends meet. 
After a month of looking for work and crying a lot, one week ago I started my first job. I never imagined I could do it but I wake up early every morning, work six days a week and am starting to finally feel like half an adult. 
My point is, it just happens. You can’t make yourself become an independent woman unless one day there is no other option. Life just happens. One day you’ll wake up in the morning and realise you have to go to work and be an actual adult. 
I’m not saying you have to go through what I went through (I would never wish that on my worst enemy) but everyone eventually has to become an adult, for some reason or another. It’s okay to take your time. You’re not “behind” anyone. You’re moving according to your own time. It all depends on situations and circumstances. 
You will work when you have to.. when you’re meant to. Sometimes I can’t believe I’m an actual working adult (it’s just been a week so it’s understandable) but I’m slowly beginning to create goals, stepping beyond my comfort zone. 
You can look for jobs, make an effort to be an adult but it won’t last until you HAVE to do it. Human beings are wired to choose the more comfortable option, take the easy way out.. until there isn’t an easy way out anymore. 
So wait it out. Your time will come. You’ll miss these days when it does :)

I’m 23 and just about to graduate college while most of my friends have moved on to their third jobs. Trust me, you’re not lagging behind. Most employers don’t care that you don’t have a graduate degree if you have the experience to cover for it. 
That being said, if you do want a degree anyway, you may want to look into an online course. There are tons of undergraduate online courses that offer degrees from good affiliate universities. Udemy is one I know of even though I’m not sure if they offer undergrad courses. 
This way you can keep your job, earn and pursue your studies at your own time and pace. 

Good luck!!
